question: What does HTML stand for?
explanation: HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language. It is a markup language that describes the structure of web pages.

question: Which part of an HTML document contains the content visible on the page?
explanation: The <body> element holds everything visible on the page. The <head> holds information about the page, such as the title and metadata.

question: Which attribute provides a text description of an image for screen readers?
explanation: The alt attribute describes the image. It is read by screen readers and shown if the image fails to load.

question: How do you create a link that jumps to the element with id="faq" on the same page?
explanation: A # followed by the id in href links to that element on the same page.

question: Which list should you use for step-by-step instructions where order matters?
explanation: <ol> creates an ordered (numbered) list, which is ideal when the order of items matters.

question: Why should every form input have a connected <label>?
options: It is required for the form to submit
It tells users and screen readers what the input is for, and clicking it focuses the input
explanation: Labels describe inputs for everyone, are announced by screen readers, and enlarge the clickable area by focusing the input when clicked.

question: Is browser form validation (like required or pattern) enough to keep bad data out of your server?
options: No, it can be bypassed, so the server must validate too
explanation: Client-side validation improves user experience, but anyone can bypass it. Always validate on the server as well.

question: Which element should wrap the main, unique content of a page?
explanation: <main> represents the dominant content of the page. Use only one visible <main> per page.

question: What is the best element to use for a clickable action like "Open menu"?
explanation: A <button> is keyboard-focusable and announced as a button by screen readers. A clickable div is not accessible by default.
